samples.summary: Connector export drops the `dash` the new importer now reads, making connector round-trips lossy
samples.evidence: `parseShapeStroke` is shared by connectors: `packages/slides/src/import/pptx/shape.ts:1054` (inside `parseCxnSp`) calls it, so after this change an imported `<p:cxnSp>` whose `<a:ln>` carries `<a:prstDash val="dash"/>` arrives as `stroke.dash: 'dashed'` and is painted dashed by `connector-renderer.ts:50`. But the connector exporter builds its line by hand — `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/connector.ts:102-110` emits `<a:ln w=…>{solidFill}{headEnd}{tailEnd}</a:ln>` and never consults `stroke.dash` (it does not use `lineXml`, which is the only place `DASH_VAL`/`<a:prstDash>` is written, `export/pptx/shape.ts:152`). So import→export→import silently converts every dashed connector to solid. The round-trip suite does not catch it: the only connector fixture, `test/import/pptx/__fixtures__/build-rich-pptx.ts:373`, has no `<a:prstDash>`, and the new round-trip case added in this diff covers shapes only. Fix belongs in `connector.ts` (emit `<a:prstDash>`, ideally by reusing `lineXml`), or the importer should not record `dash` for connectors.
searchedFor: grep parseShapeStroke call sites in packages/slides/src/import

samples.summary: Table cell borders still ignore `<a:prstDash>`, so shapes/connectors and table edges now disagree about dash fidelity
samples.evidence: `parseCellBorder` returns `{ color, width }` (`packages/slides/src/import/pptx/table.ts:222-223`) with no `prstDash` handling, and the table exporter likewise writes `<a:ln{side} w=…>` without a dash (`packages/slides/src/export/pptx/table.ts:120`) — yet `table-renderer.ts:314` already paints `dashArray(edge.stroke.dash, edge.stroke.width)`. Symmetric today (nothing is lost on round trip), so it still works, but the new `DASH_BY_PRST` table now exists only on the shape path; a dashed PowerPoint table border keeps importing as solid while the identical border on a rectangle does not.

samples.summary: Hardcoded `setLineDash([6, 4])` is now only the width-1 special case of `dashArray('dashed', w)`
samples.evidence: `drawImageFailurePlaceholder` sets `ctx.lineWidth = 1; ctx.setLineDash([6, 4])` (packages/slides/src/view/canvas/image-renderer.ts:147-148) rather than going through the shared helper. It renders identically today because the width is 1, but it is a literal duplicate of the base ratio that this change made width-relative, so it will drift if the placeholder stroke ever thickens or the ratios move.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. `parseShapeStroke` (packages/slides/src/import/pptx/shape.ts:1005-1026) now returns `dash` from `<a:prstDash>`, and `parseCxnSp` calls it at line 1054 and spreads the stroke onto the ConnectorElement unmodified at line 1070; `ConnectorElement.stroke` is `ShapeStroke` = `Stroke`, which carries `dash?` (model/connector.ts:33, model/element.ts:160-167). The connector exporter builds `<a:ln>` by hand at export/pptx/connector.ts:105-110 using only width, color and arrowheads — it never reads `stroke.dash` and never calls `lineXml`. `<a:prstDash>` is emitted in exactly one place in src/, export/pptx/shape.ts:151-153 inside `lineXml`, whose only call sites are shape.ts:198 and shape.ts:243 (shape and text), not the connector path. `connectorToXml` has a single caller, export/pptx/group.ts:71, and no other code injects prstDash, so there is no alternate connector export path preserving dash. The loss is observable because the connector renderer honours dash (view/canvas/stroke-dash.test.ts:146-178 asserts drawConnector sets dashed/dotted patterns). Test coverage does not catch it: the dash round-trip case at test/export/pptx/round-trip.test.ts:241-280 filters on `el.type === 'shape'`, and test/export/pptx/connector.test.ts contains no dash assertion. Result: an imported dashed connector silently becomes solid on export/re-import. This is a behaviour change to a shared symbol whose other consumer was not updated — in-lane for blast-radius, major (silently drops work/state on a reachable path). No counterexample found.
